projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Jack Blank was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Think we're good?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: All right. I don't even know like where to start out.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Well, were you drafted or enlisted?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: I enlisted.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You enlisted?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: I was only 17 years old, yeah. They didn't draft you that young.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How old did you have to be to be drafted?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And you enlisted when you were 17?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Umhum. I quit school to go. I would have flunked probably because I had skipped school to go see Elaine all that time.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You were skipping school to go see Elaine?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Were you guys just dating then?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How old you were you when you guys got married?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: About 26--no--22.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You were in the war?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No, the war was over.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: World War II was over.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah but the other ones were still, you know.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: But we were going together at 13.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How old was she?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: 13, and we started going together.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And you were 17?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No, I was 13 too.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh. So you guys had been together for like, four years.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What'd she think about you going to the war?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: What could she do? She gets ready for me.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did she get sad?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, it was sad. She wrote to me almost every day though.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you save them?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Some of them. See I couldn't write to her because we couldn't write for 60 days we were at sea. And we didn't have no way to mail it so she got to wait until I came in and then she'd get a bunch of them at one time. It was-- it was neat.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It was--that's sad though.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Were you living at home at the time?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Why did you join?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: I told you I was going to flunk in school. No, I was patriotic. I wanted to do my part in the war.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What did your parents think about that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: They didn't like it but they signed for me. I had to get my parents to sign for me so I could go when I was 17.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Why didn't your dad go?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: My--he wasn't home. They were separated and he-- I didn't know where he was, so my mother took care of me.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What about boot camp and training?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Boot camp was--was Chicago and I tried to get in the Navy when I was 17 and they told me I couldn't get in the first time I tried-- enlisted because I had a ___+. The second--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What does that have to do with anything?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, that's what I told them. I said I ain't going to fight the Japs. So the second-- the second time they said okay, they'd take me but I'd never get in the submarines. So then I went to boot camp and they had a 10 mile march coming up at boot camp and they said except for those guys who want to volunteer for submarines they won't have to go on the march. I said I wanted to make submarines anyhow so I'll volunteer.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Three days later I was on a train going to New London, Connecticut Submarine School. So I spent six months at submarine school. And then when I graduated from there I was assigned to the Gavelin at Redding, Connecticut. That's where built it. And then I went to the pacific. I stopped in Florida, my brother-in-law was on a submarine chaser in Florida. And we went down there for practice. And he was on one of the chasers that gave us--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: He was in war too?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. And he was on a submarine chaser that did depth charges so we'd get used to what it was like. And so then I went over to Panama Canal to Pearl Harbor. And we went out on our first patrol. And I came back to Pearl and I spent two weeks at the Royal Hawaiian Hotel to rest and then we went out and then I came back and we went to Brixton, Australia. I went to the mountains of Tulumba for two weeks to rest there. And then I went out and we came back for the (?pre mantle?). And I went to the shore for two weeks rest. And I went out again on another patrol and came back to the Philippines. And we got two weeks rest there. And Gaby met a-- Gaby, that was our dog, we had a dog and he was a male-- and the Gar was another submarine. They had a female dog called (gargle) And they met in the Philippines and we got a radio message on the next war patrol that Gaby was the proud father of one pup.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Aw!

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: So Gaby was a father, so--a lot of the boats had pets.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Mascots?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, mascots. But, Gaby he was--he was a good dog and you saw his picture.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Never did a mess on the boat.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Where'd you guys get him?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Dog pound in Pearl Harbor.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You just picked him out?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, we just went and got him. Never made a mess on the submarine.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Where'd he go to the bathroom?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Up on the cigarette deck up on the ___ tower the Captain would take him up with him at night and he'd do his business.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Cigarette deck?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. And then we'd take him down in the morning because we'd dive as soon as the sun come up and we'd stay down all day. And we would take him down with us. And during depth charge when it got real hot he'd lay by the icebox door—there was a little icebox and you could see the cold air coming out and he'd lay there with his nose right up against it. Got any room there yet or are we done?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: No, we're good.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: We got--we got like a good half an hour.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And ol' Gaby was with us and every time we'd go to the rest camp we'd take him to the kennels and give him a bath and a hair cut. And--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How many of there were you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: 75 men and ten officers made up the crew. And we carried 24 torpedoes and 117,000 gallons of fuel oil.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: On a submarine?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. That was on tanks all around the outside. And we went to sea and we'd go out until our food was gone, our fuel was gone, or our torpedoes were gone. And they'd give us a square in the ocean and we'd stay in that square. You know--they'd tell us what the coordinates were. We'd stay in that square and anything that came through that we'd sink. [interview interrupted by a telephone call]

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And, okay, so where was I? Elaine: Who was that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: May--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It's okay.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Jill, looking for Penny.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You were saying how on the outside of the ship, the fuel and all that.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Okay anything that came through that square we would sink. Because--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Anything?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Anything, yeah. Because nobody--none of our ships were supposed to be there.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So how many ships did you sink?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Nine. We sank the--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Were they Japanese, or--

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, yeah. We sank four Japanese metal wars. That's like destroyers. We sank the last cruiser of the war, the Japanese cruiser. It had 4,000 army troops on it and plus the crew through the Navy and that was us in the pursuit of it together in the wolf pack and we sank it and there wasn't a survivor on it. We went back up looking and there wasn't a survivor.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: At all?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Not one known person. It went down fast.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So you saw those dead bodies?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No, there--we didn't see any bodies--or anything. We didn't see nothing. The ship we hit—Gavelin blew the bow off of it. It was the diamond--what we call diamond throat shot and we fired the torpedoes out and we blew the bow off. And it was going forward so then they started going down. And the other boat put six torpedoes in it. And so it just sank just like that.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: One of your boats?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, yeah. We were in what they call a wolf pack. When two or more boats went out to get it they call that a wolf pack. They went together.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And we did the lifeguard duty on Tokyo Bay the--the pilots from the aircraft carriers-- the one that bombed Japan-- they'd know where we were at. They'd--they'd tell them that we were going to be along the Tokyo Bay there. And if they got in trouble and they couldn't make it back to their carrier, that they were to ditch in Tokyo Bay and ____...(3 seconds).

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: They had other planes up there that when they ditched they'd protect us because we couldn't dive in there. We were on the surf--we had to stay on the surface. And that guy that we'd picked up here--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: That was one of your guys.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, that was--he--there was ten aircraft that came off his carrier and none of them survived. And none of them came back to the carrier, they all crashed in Tokyo Bay and we went in 31 miles to pick him up and when he was in his life raft he said that he could hear a woman open the door and let a dog out on the shore. And when we went in to get him to the shore batteries opened up and fired at us while we were on the surface. But we got out in time. But then we were supposed to--they told us to get out because the fleet was going to come in and bomb Japan. But the Captain saw--we saw this guy here. We saw him in there and the Captain says I can see him he says I'm not going to leave him there because the Japanese will come out in boats trying to get him, too.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: They were just trying to kill him?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. So he said we're going in after him. And when we were supposed to get out, because the fleet was going to come in and bomb the shore. And then the storm came up so we come in and we got him and we got him aboard and we were coming out the fleet had come in because we didn't make it out of there in time like we were supposed to. So then they started shelling us. And they depth charged us for eight hours--they--they thought we were Japanese submarines.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Your--wait, you're guys were doing this to you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, our fleet was doing this to us.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Shooting at you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. It was--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Because they thought it was Japanese?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Friendly fire is what they call it. Yeah. They thought we were a Japanese submarine. And of course we were Americans.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Well, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: But, finally after eight hours they finally-- we got a recognition signal out that they could see and then they quit--they quit. And then--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Nobody was injured with that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Was anybody injured during that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No, no we scared them.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And what bothered me more about being in Tokyo Bay then anything is our airplanes dropped mines all over in there to sink Japanese ships.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And in the daytime, when we were in there we'd sink about 20, 30 mines with gunfire because we'd see them floating there. But at night, we'd surface and we'd been all over the place and we'd never see a mine. And I'd sit there and I'd say, man. Something's wrong here. But I guess I lived, right? Because I made it back and that was it.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: That was the end of the war then. There was--submarines were less then one percent of the Navy. And they sank 52 percent of the Japanese fleet. And we lost one in five men in the submarines so we lost 52 submariners all together.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: American subs?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And how many were actually out?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, by the end of the war we had about 200 out.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So like 100 some still were fine?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How many Americans were killed?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How many Japanese were killed?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, this is just submarine people.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: This is just submarine people is the only, you know. There was 3,000 submariners killed. And I belong to Submarine Veterans of World War II we go to all kinds of meetings now. We're real close and--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So you know all your guys that were--

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Oh, yeah. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Are you friends with them?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: We--yeah, we have reunions every year. There's one out in--coming up in June in Boston--in Niagara Falls. Yeah, we go to them all. And these guys are down in Bucyrus I go down there second Monday--or second Saturday of every month and we have breakfast in a restaurant down there.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Aw.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And there's 28 guys come down there. So we're--we're a close-knit bunch.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So there were 75 on your submarine?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Seventy-five men and ten officers.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And how many survived throughout the whole thing?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, everybody.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Everybody survived?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And then, yours like--they're not all alive now, are they?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No, no. We're down to--I think there's only 35 of us left.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you have like best friends in the war?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Oh yeah. Oh yeah. Yeah, in fact he lived in Cleveland. And he just passed away a couple years ago. But we were just like brothers. We still write to each other all of us. One guy sends a letter out every quarter about what's happening--like I told him Elaine was sick and I told them about this. In fact, I sent this to him and he's the guy that sends out that letter. And he copied it out and sent it to everybody at a gathering. So, but that's a good looking dog, ain't it?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It is, oh it's so cute.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How long did the dog live?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: After the war, why, they raffled him off. And the guy that won him took him home--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Is this a guy from the war?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, he called up the Captain and says I can't keep him because he's homesick. He needs all the people so the Captain put him back on another submarine. And so, I don't know when he passed away. He was back in it. And that's it, Jessica. [interview interrupted by Elaine] Elaine: You guy's done yet?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Oh man.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What about, what about all the other--okay.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Okay what?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Hold on.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you stay in touch with your family when you were in the war? Did you stay in touch with your family?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you write them?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yep. [interview interrupted by Elaine] Elaine: Jess, you want some Diet Coke?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Sure, thanks. Elaine: It's decaf.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah, that's fine. Yeah. Elaine: You want ice in it?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yes, please. Thank you.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, I wrote to them. And Elaine wrote to me. My mother wrote to me.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Elaine you're so sweet. Elaine: Yeah I was.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you miss him when he was in the war?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: She can't hear me.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Did you hear her Elaine? Elaine: No.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: She asked if you missed me when the war was on. Elaine: No, why would I miss him?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Don't lie.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What was the food like?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: It was good on submarines. But we were out of fresh-- fresh food about 20 days after we were out and then we had canned goods and--yuck.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yuck.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And when we left Australia, why we had mutton for--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What is that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: It's sheep.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: We had that every day for the whole patrol. Boy, it-- I can't stand mutton like that.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Eww, gross.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You don't eat it anymore, do you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And we had ice-- we had ice cream machine and we showed movies. And when we showed all the movies we had on board we'd radio another submarine and we'd meet them out in the middle of the ocean and exchange movies. We'd take their movies and give them our movies. And then we'd go out to get them--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: What kind of movies did you watch?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Regular movies that were in the show. I mean in the--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Like what-- I mean it was like--

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, one of them was Destination Tokyo.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh. [interview inturrupted by Elaine]

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Thank you. Elaine: You're welcome.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And White Christmas and all that--any kind of movie.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Was it in black-and-white?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. And then when we'd go to rest camp why the red cross girls would come and they'd-- we'd play ball and that and they'd ask us if they'd want them to write to our parents and tell them how we were and everything.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did they?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: That's what I was just going to ask you.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: But the two weeks that we had a rest camp was fabulous. I mean, man we'd--we didn't have no--it was just like you were on vacation because you didn't have no rules or nothing. I mean, you were on your own. We had like a motel with rooms where--two guys to a room. In Aus--in Pearl Harbor we stayed at the Royal Hawaiian Hotel and they had a price list for the doors, the slats how much it was a dollar a slat, for breaking slats. And the mirrors and they had prices for everything you broke so you had to pay it. And I shouldn't say this--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It's okay.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: We used to--the Captain used to give each division like Engine Men, Quarter Masters and that-- he'd give them a five can of Gilly-- what we called Gilly was torpedo alcohol. And we'd mix it with pineapple juice and run it through bread to take the color out of it.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you get drunk?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Oh-oh.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Real drunk?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Real bad.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Was that when you were on your vacation?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you guys drink a lot when you were, like--

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you guys smoke?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Some of them did, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Do you--did you smoke?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: I didn't smoke, no. But, you just drank because everybody else drank.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: There was nothing to do, was there?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No, no it was bad. And then when we were in Pearl Harbor why the submarine sailors got to stay out all night. We were privileged. I mean, they really looked after us.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: They were really, really good to us. But the other ships had to be back in at midnight.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You guys didn't have a curfew?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You guys were spoiled.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. And when we went to Australia, man that was something else. That--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Why is that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: That was just like the states, I mean, you walk down the street and you'd see three girls coming. You put your arm out and they'd hang on--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: I was going to ask that about the girls, like where they like--?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. Submarine sailors, we get extra money. We got 50 percent extra pay. For being on a submarine. So the girls knew--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You guys had money.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: --had money and cigarettes.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did they flirt with you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah, well, yeah. You could have any girl you want just because you were a sailor. I mean--well all their boyfriends were gone to the jungle. We called them diggers and they were all gone. But at the rest camps they used to bring buses like the rest camp was just like a motel and they had like a buffet supper and beer.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And they'd bring girls up by the busload and they'd have the dance and you know, it was pretty nice.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It's like the movies.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It's like the movies.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And it was like that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. It was weird.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you dance with those girls?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, sure you did. Well you--we're alive aren't we? I mean, you know we're--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did you think Elaine would be mad?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: She's had brought a couple ____ home. She didn't sit home all the time either. Don't let her tell you--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did girls like you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Did girls like you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: They like everybody. They liked any Americans. They were-- we had money. I went to one rest camp and I bought a horse for a carton of cigarettes.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Are you kidding me?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: This girl says I know a real good restaurant. So I bought the horses for a carton of cigarettes was going to take a ride on them. Walked those god darn horses all day long my rear end was so sore. Got there and the-- the restaurant had burned down.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh my gosh.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Didn't have nothing to--to eat.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: And your butt was sore.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Do you remember the day your service ended?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Where were you?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Rota, Spain. On--but this is when I retired from the Navy. Yeah, I retired from the nuclear power submarine, changed enrollments. And it was in Rota, Spain. And then they flew me back to the states. I got a family gram-- I made one patrol on the nuclear-- you still got tape left?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum. It's an hour.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: I mean, we don't have to go for the hour.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Okay. Am I doing all right?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: I ain't hogging you am I?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: No. I like hearing this.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Okay, on the nuclear powered submarine we couldn't send out, see? I dove off of Charleston, South Carolina and surfaced off of Rota, Spain three months later. We never came up for three months. We stayed under for three months.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh my gosh.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And, I couldn't send letters out but Elaine could send the family gram to me. And that was-- she was allowed up to 20 words. And the first one she bought was, or sent to me was in--in buying the farm. And the second one was we're on the farm, painting like mad. And then the third one was hurry home, we're on the farm. We're all set. So--so I owe everything to her. I really do. Because she's took care of the kids, she did all the bills--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So you had kids while--

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Well, on the nuclear power submarine. Not during the war. We weren't married. We were married after the war. But then I went on nuclear power. And I'd be gone for three months and then I'd be in for three months. Then I'd be gone for three months and she did all this on her own with the kids and everything because I was gone most of the time.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And she took care getting this farm and did all that so I owe her a lot.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Here?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: How long have you lived here?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Her uncle--56 years--her uncle had this farm and we used to come out here in the summer and I'd come home on leave and we'd come out here and help because he lived alone. And I always told him if he sold the farm I wanted to buy it. And so she took care of everything while I was gone.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Jack's love story. Nobody's going to hear this, are they?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: It's going to be in the Library of Congress. You just signed that paper.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Oh. But I'll tell you what, it was hard during the war. But I'd do it in a heartbeat again to get to this.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: You know I was just a kid just--just your age and I was running a--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: That'd be like me going to war.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: I can't picture that.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And I'm running a big submarine like that at that age. Any average age on there was 18, 19 years old.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: So all your friends were like 18, 19?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah, there was a couple of older guys on the there but the majority of them were all 18, 19 year-olds. All young kids. And you had two captains during the war the-- the first one only made one patrol and the other one made five and we all liked him. We don't want anyone-- see-- he was smart and he knew what he was doing.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. Someday I'll have to show you my scrapbook from nuclear power and we had to--that was something. Now there isn't too many people-- now Elaine, she was on the nuclear power submarine.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: She went to sea on it.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And Barbara did, too. And Craig did but Penny didn't, she was too young and they wouldn't let her on. But they went to sea on the nuclear power submarine before we went out overseas. And so there isn't too many people that were on diesel boats and electric boats like I was and I qualified on both of them. So I have a combat pin for World War II and I have a pin for nuclear power for patrol on a nuclear power submarine. Not many people have that.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: You're the man.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Yeah. Admiral Rickover-- you get a submarine combat pin, you know, during the war you get stars for each battle.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Umhum.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: And when I was on the James Monroe-- that was the nuclear power one-- Admiral Rickover came through and he saw my combat--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Who was that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Who's that?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: He's the father of nuclear power. He--he was an admiral. And he's the big mahoof for nuclear power.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: But he came through and inspected the troops and there was only two people on there that had the World War II combat pins and he stopped and he talked to me for about five minutes and the Captain was nervous as a cat because an Admiral just don't talk to enlisted men like that, you know.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: He talked to the other guy, too, for the same time and he said that he needed guys like us on nuclear power submarines. So he was--

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: Impressed?

sp.speaker: Jack Blank
sp.p: I'm pretty proud of it, yeah. So, that's it.

sp.speaker: Jessica Gore
sp.p: We're good.
